query:
In a recent study, a group of subjects had their normal daily caloric intake increased by 25 percent. This increase was entirely in the form of alcohol. Another group of similar subjects had alcohol replace nonalcoholic sources of 25 percent of their normal daily caloric intake. All subjects gained body fat over the course of the study, and the amount of body fat gained was the same for both groups.

An increased amount of body fat does not necessarily imply a weight gain is most strongly supported by the information above.
predicted_answer: Increased body fat does not necessarily imply weight gain

The Global Context Preview clearly states that "All subjects gained body fat over the course of the study..." which implies an increase in body fat without necessarily indicating an increase in weight.

FINAL ANSWER: Increased body fat does not necessarily imply weight gain
